ratings.comment: Really bad professor

I've never given a 1/5 and I hate to, but it has to be done. Lectures are extremely confusing, both in terms of slides and Prof's explanation. He dosen't engage well with his students, deadlines and direction of the course are not clear to us. Not much guidance is provided so much that most students just end up giving the bare minimum.

Yu Hen Hu clearly understands his topics and is passionate about them but there is a large disconnect between him and his students. He is extremely hard to understand and does not do a good job of facilitating an understanding of any content. He loves to throw a multitude of formulas on the screen at once and then quickly move on.

Prof. Hu is friendly and highly knowledgeable about ML, but he tends to explain things in a way that makes them more confusing. That being said, 532 is more or less a self-study class, with pre-recorded lecture videos by Prof Van Veen, so the instructor doesn't matter that much. It's tough to get an A with a cutoff of 92.
This prof has everything but two tests be participation based, and then has the audacity to curve the class harshly. Very few students get A's, and even fewer learn anything. Steer clear.
Do not take Yu Hen Hu. What ever you do take someone else. He just throws up random slides with variables and his lectures make no sense. DO NOT TAKE

Do not take this class if you have Yu Hen Hu! Drop immediately, go take 540 it has way better professors.This dude's lectures make no sense, he just throws complicated equations at you and expects you to understand. You will have to learn everything by yourself if you expect to do good in this class. AGAIN, DO NOT TAKE YU HEN HU.
His lectures are pointless and make no sense. You are better off just learning about ANN's on your own.

He copy/pastes most of the code examples and lecture slides that we use from popular websites for Machine Learning. This makes his lectures confusing be he is trying to explain another persons work.
I got 100% on all hws and exercises, close to the top score on the midterm and final, and slightly above average on the final project yet I got an AB.

I want to like Prof. Hu, but I can't. His lectures consist of him lecturing on the same 6 slides for 50 minutes, while he largely reads from the slides. Additionally, the exercises are typically copy-and-paste exercises, and the completion-based nature of assignments gives little motivation to learn. If you are looking for an AI course, take 540.

Lectures and lecture slides are made to confuse you even more than you probably already are. Minimal feedback given back on homework and in-class exercises. Midterm had an average of 57%. Avoid this professor at all costs, you will learn absolutely nothing

Definitely avoid this class if you are new to AI! It will ruin your passion. The professor doesn't have a good understanding of the materials and is careless about his students. If you go to office hours he just talks about general stuff, standing up like he's leaving. The slides and lectures make little sense, better read clearer online blogs.

His lectures are useless, basically just reads off the slides. The slides make no sense whatsoever and tend to confuse you even more than you probably already are. Do not take this class if you haven't taken linear algebra. Would not recommend this class

The professor provides little to no feedback on in-class assignments and homework. The lecture slides are unclear and no common naming convention is followed. Grading for graduate students is very tough (>94 for an A) and the final was a 16+ page coding assignment that took almost 3 days to complete.

Terrible professor. The lecture is useless and he just read through the slide, so no one really shows up. Take-home final exam is 18 pages long and needs around 2 full days to finish. Complete waste of time and money.

Taking class as a graduate student you needed to score a 95% or higher in the class for an A. Considering no feedback is given on anything this is near impossible since the final exam was 18 pages long, worth 30% of final grade, and had to be revised nearly 10 times due to errors found by students. This class was a waste of my time and money.

Took ECE 539 as a grad student and was probably one of my worst experiences in school to date. Going into the final week of class I had a 99.9% in the class (high score on midterm and 100% on all homeworks and exercises). In the day grades are due the professor puts 60% of the points in (final exam and project) with no feedback dropping me to AB.

Dr. Hu is a very kind professor and an excellent lecturer. Having said that, I would not take his course without being very good at either Python or Matlab. I would highly recommend CS540 as a prerequisite for this class because that class, to a degree, holds your hand on how to code NNs in Python.

Alright class. Lectures: mid. I took this after CS 540, and if I hadnt taken it, I'd be lost. The classes went over a lot of the same things except my professors for 540 were way better at explaining things. Overall, you do learn a lot, but Id say 540 is the better class. Also the (take home) final is absurd. 10+ hours of extra work in finals week.

One of the best classes I've ever taken. Very application-based, building ML models (MATLAB or Python) instead of getting bogged down with the math. He presents all that as well, it just goes way over my head. As for Yu Hen, man is he quick and a wealth of knowledge. Talked with me for 30 minutes giving me inspired tips on my final project.

The professor is super kind and friendly, he is also willing to listen to student feedbacks. But this course is too difficult. The content of two lectures could easily take another whole course to learn. I know the professor does not expect us to master these contents, but we also have little clue how good we should get to pass the course.

If you want to keep your GPA, do not take this course. Too much homework, and the time you spent on your homework does not match the score. Exam is tough as well, you even cannot finish it. In this course you just watch video and study by yourself just like an online course. But this course is really important for CS students, so work hard.
I loved 203 with Yu Hu! The exams were exactly like the review and he made himself very approachable. I really enjoyed him this semester!!

203 is a WISCEL class, so Prof Hu didn't end up lecturing at all. He made himself very accessible to all of the students and is overall a very nice man. I had a great experience with the class and am very thankful to have had such an approachable professor. He can sometimes be a little confusing when trying to explain things, but it ended up okay

This class didn't give any chance to practice problems so you basically had to learn entire concepts from a couple examples from videos and one or two homework problems. Labs were very hard to follow and complete. Would not recommend... I put way too much time into a 3 credit course. Maybe the in person version is better but who knows.

Yu Hu is overall a very nice man, but he cannot explain the material at all. He would oftentimes make me more confused than I was prior to asking him a question. So, I would NOT recommend taking this course with him as he will make it way more difficult than it should be. The TAs were far more helpful than he ever was.

Super nice guy. The class is a Wiscel class where the lectures are online then you do glorified quizzes with the people at your table during class. There are also homeworks and projects which you must do with your lab partner. He is very friendly and wants to help you learn.
extremely rude, never take again

Yu is a nice guy but by god he can not teach. He is a tough grader that shows no remorse. Ex: he marked 10 points off, essentially a letter grade, on my exam because I wrote e^j(0) instead of 1 on my spectra gram. When I went to confront him of the absurdness of the situation he just shrugged his shoulders. AVOID HIM

I don't know what's wrong with this website. I wonder if people just rate their professor based on the easiness. Professor Hu is  a great professor and always help if you ask. He is also very knowledgeable and serious towards teaching. On the other hand, his grading is tough and some times he doesn't give timely homework feedback (not always).

Yu Hu is a friendly guy, however he doesn't care about the course or its students. Doctor Hu seems to think that time travel is possible, he graded our assignments after the final exam, giving us ample time to study in some kind of science fiction universe. He doesn't care, grades hard, will change clerical things and screw you. Avoid. YOOOO HOOOO!

The administration part of the class was terrible. Here's a list of reasons: 1) The video lectures were often impossible to hear, due to bad audio. 2) Homework was graded at a glacial pace. 3) Keys, for homeworks and the test, were often incorrect. 4) Regrading was handled carelessly 5) The syllabus was  often wrong and not fixed.

Students watch at least one hour-long video lecture per week outside of class. To force attendance and watching of the video(s), there's a weekly quiz and in-class exercises. The professor is very smart, but is utterly incapable of communicating even basic course concepts to students. Also, the entire course is intense math.
If you like foreign language classes, and are ready to watch long video lectures from the 80's to understand what you are suppose to be learning I highly recommend this class.

Most horribly organized class I have ever taken. "Mini-projects" easily take 40+ man-hours of work. All assignments are "peer-graded". Deadlines moved up, specifications changed daily. You will know fear if you take this class with this professor. Had to go to therapy for this class.
Never expected that this course would be handled so carelessly. Do not enroll in this course if   Hu is teaching.

Gives unclear and bad explanations about material. Hence its same as attending or missing lectures. Makes bad jokes in class. Does a peer grading in which students grade each other and can see the names of the ppl they r grading which can cause partiality. The only way one can learn is self studying in this class. Better take CS 552 with karu

Horrible lecturer; doesn't go over material in an organized fashion at all.  Homework answer keys change on an hourly basis, drop boxes are opened mere hours before due dates and the students are required to grade each other even though the class is curved!

His lectures are not clear. Have to study on your own. Home work problems are also not clear and he changes the solutions so many times. Better to take ECE552 when it is being offered by CS department

Please Avoid!!! Take ECE 552 when offered by the CS department. The homework problems are vague and so are the midterms and final exams. He barely explains stuff properly and gives weird interpretations related to hamburgers and hotdogs. Lectures are boring and worthless. Projects are based on Quartus.

I think the reason he teach is that he try to show students he is the experts in the field. Don't care about students' opinion at all. If you propose something, he will always dismiss it by saying a incomprehensible concepts which he only knows but no one else did. Also, bad at explaining stuff..
Meaningless lectures and tough grade on Quartus Project.

Somewhat easy, but his lectures ramble and aren't very useful (you are going to have to teach yourself the material whether or not you attend class). The homework questions are sometimes incomprehensible  - though many are taken straight from the book/previous semesters. Have to use Quartus for the project - TAKE IN THE CS DEPARTMENT AND NOT ECE.
Stay away. Lectures were not instructive or helpful. I did well in this class only because I was able to sit in on Joe Krachey's lectures.
Useless, all I remember is that theres something that happens on "THE NEXT CLOCK CYCLE." Super boring and not helpful.

Horrible.  Lecture is rambling to power point.  No examples.  Homework is ~ 9 vague questions pulled out of thin air that he doesn't even know the answers to and 1 design problem that he doesn't even grade.  You're grade in this class will depend on how well you can guess at what he wants the homework questions to mean.  Never does design examples.

His primary method of explaining concepts is fast food analogies.  Makes mistakes on answer keys, had trouble understanding why my final project wasn't as slow as he expected. Skip lectures, teach yourself the material from the book, and hope he doesn't ask about McDonald's out of order execution framework on an exam. avoid.

As others have said, there's no reason to go to his lectures unless you want to learn about hotdogs. Midterm and Final are only vaguely based off lecture/homework. He consistently makes mistakes on answer keys, which translates to inaccurate homework grades (and final grades too I imagine... ). AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Lectures are totally worthless, just read the book as his lectures and homework all are based off it. A bit hard to understand. I have found him to be unfriendly and unhelpful in office hours as well.

As the other comment says, he was an engaging speaker for the first bit of the semester. After that, he just either lost interest in life or wanted to die or some such, because his lectures became so boring I stopped going outright. Never was a really good teacher; expect to learn from the book for the vast majority of what you do in this class.

The first 2/3 of the semester were pretty good. He was very engaging and taught the material well. But the last 1/3 he completely lost the entire class, he would spend days going over an example that wasn't that difficult. Overall he was a decent prof but I would avoid him if possible.
A bit hard to understand. Loud and boring lectures, impossible to learn complicated things in.  Very hard projects and exams in this class regardless of teacher.

Might be a bit hard to understand because of his chinese accent, but aside from that he's a great teacher! Attempts to make jokes in class so it makes lecture interesting. Tests are easy if you understand the homework and look over the book. Going to lecture isn't really necessary.
